verdict: No remaining mathematical correctness blocker found in reviewed change. Previous coincident/moving-zero-ray cancellation counterexamples now decline while valid constant-angle branches retain zero derivatives.
mathematical_basis: Three-point Angle uses original atan2(abs(det(u,v)),dot(u,v)) exactly, on nonzero rays.
Two-line Angle uses atan2(abs(det(n1,n2)),abs(dot(n1,n2))), equal to original acos(abs(normalized_dot)) for nonzero normals; values lie in[0,pi/2].
Derivatives on each smooth branch share denominator det^2+dot^2 rather than a cancellation-prone 1-cos^2 expression.
Retaining both ray/normal squared norms before simplification prevents an undefined angle from disappearing when atan2 or the full residual simplifies.
Abs branch cusps conservatively decline; known constant-angle parameterizations remain differentiable away from zero rays/normals.
Jacobian plans remain optional Newton proposals; original residual, domain, independent final verification and exact answer contracts are untouched.

coverage: Moving collinear/parallel/perpendicular constant-angle families, both signs,80/180/500dps.
Zero ray/normal excluded at x=0 while valid x in{-2,-1,1,2} returns zero derivatives.
0*Angle and sin(Angle) cannot erase the moving angle domain.
Named scalar angle aliases, exact row cancellation, and angle expressions on the equality RHS retain domain obligations.
